incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGERDUTY ALERT PDINC12345 - Auth service: token verification spike. Trigger: token-verify-error-rate > 5% in prod/eu-west1. Link: <https://pagerduty.example/PDINC12345>

pagerduty-bot: Paging @alex (primary oncall) -> escalation policy: auth-team -> sec-oncall (if not acked in 5m)

alex: acking. i'm on it. pulling logs now.

alex: quick tail from auth-service (eu-west1):
```
2026-03-14T18:04:12Z ERROR token_verify: signature_verification_failed kid=k-2026 token_id=xa3f...
2026-03-14T18:04:13Z WARN jwks_cache: requested_kid_not_found kid=k-2026 cache_version=42
```

maria: seeing broad 401s on customer login and API token auth. Graphs: token_verify_error_rate spiked to 18% 18:03->18:07. Affected: payment checkout, ingestion endpoints. Region: eu-west1 primarily.

sean: any recent deploys or key rotations in the last 30m? I can check deploy history.

ops_lead: i did a manual key rotation job earlier for a canary, not prod. No prod deploys scheduled. but there was a config push to auth-config-store ~12m ago.

alex: traces show tokens with kid=k-2026 while several auth instances have JWKS containing only k-2025. looks like partial JWKS propagation / stale cache. possible race during key rollout.

incident-bot: Escalating to sec-oncall after 4m without resolution.

sec-oncall: joining. can someone dump the JWKS that auth instances are using? we need to confirm propagation vector (cache vs config-store vs env).

maria: fetched jwk from instance-a-1 (eu-west1): contains only k-2025. fetched jwk from instance-b-3 (eu-west1): contains k-2026. inconsistent.

alex: hypothesis: config-store update reached some hosts but not all; auth-service caches JWKS in local memory + redis invalidation not firing. If tokens issued by the new signing key (k-2026) arrive at instances with old jwks they fail verify.

sean: mitigation options: 1) roll back to previous signing key (if possible) 2) force JWKS reload across fleet (restart or endpoint cache flush) 3) enable temporary tolerant verification (not ideal).

ops_lead: we should avoid lenient verification. plan: force JWKS reload by triggering rolling restart of auth pods in eu-west1 to clear local caches. i'll hand off restart to @sean. notify customers.

sean: executing rolling restart now: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/auth-service -n prod --selector=region=eu-west1`

alex: monitoring token verify error rate and 5xx/401 logs.

sre-duty: FYI adding a short alert annotation: all calls to /v1/auth/verify with header x-auth-token return 401 -> sample rate/percent.

(2 minutes pass)

pagerduty-bot: PDINC12345 acknowledged by alex at 18:07 UTC. Escalation paused.

sean: restart in progress; 6/24 pods restarted, restarting 4 more.

maria: starting to see drop in error rate in eu-west1; 401s down from 18% -> ~6%.

alex: logs after restart show JWKS now consistent across sampled pods.

sean: rollout finished. all auth-service pods in eu-west1 restarted and report jwks containing both k-2025 and k-2026.

pagerduty-bot: PDINC12345 status changed: resolved by sean at 18:15 UTC.

maria: metrics: token_verify_error_rate stable ~0.9% (baseline ~0.3%). customer-support: reported two customers who saw transient failures; both confirm services back to normal.

customer-support: sending post-incident notice to affected customers now. template used and individual follow-ups queued.

ops_lead: preliminary RCA: stale local JWKS cache + delayed cache invalidation during key rollout. Rotation process did not guarantee atomic propagation; some hosts served old keys while tokens with new kid were active.

alex: action items: 1) add atomic rollout for JWKS (publish then issue tokens after propagation window OR dual-key acceptance by token issuer), 2) add alert when percent verify failures > 5% for >2m, 3) add a /health endpoint check that verifies presence of current signing kids in JWKS.

sec-oncall: suggest adding a preflight that validates new key propagation before switching active signing key. also consider centralizing JWKS behind cache layer with pub/sub invalidation.

maria: assigning follow-ups: @ops_lead to own rollout fixes, @alex to add health check + alert, @sean to create runbook steps for forced reload and safe rollbacks.

maria: marking incident resolved. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:

alex: adding notes to incident tracker PDINC12345 and creating follow-up ticket AUTH-3472 for JWKS rollout improvements.

(incident-bot): Incident PDINC12345 closed. Summary and follow-up ticket links: <https://pagerduty.example/PDINC12345> <https://tracker.example/AUTH-3472>
